primary_sources.title: Keep the Proof State Live: Snapshotting for Efficient Tactic Search in Lean 4

claim_checks.claim: Repeated branch startup dominates wall time in the paper's stock fallback substrate.
claim_checks.evidence: Snapshot-DSP v2 reports import loading about 60 s per branch plus theorem-body elaboration estimated 18-735 s, together >99% of per-branch wall time in its standard single-machine fallback. Representative Table 2 rows report 99.9-100% overhead, with tactic CPU averaging about 45 ms across the shown 16 cases.
claim_checks.scope: This is the paper's rebuild-per-branch Lean 4 + Mathlib / lake-build fallback on an Apple M-series MacBook Pro with 8 GB RAM, not a universal Lean runtime fact. The 18-735 s theorem-body range is estimated/back-computed rather than a direct independent instrumentation of theorem-body elaboration.

claim_checks.evidence: The 45 hand-crafted Prove-phase miniF2F-v2 benchmarks show group ranges containing the 5.6x minimum and 50.0x maximum; all-45 average is 14.0x and the paper reports median 9.7x. Three separate end-to-end DSP runs show 13.2x, 13.5x, and 19.9x.
claim_checks.scope: The large range is primarily Prove-phase infrastructure timing on hand-crafted sketches specifically designed so at least one portfolio tactic closes each hole. The paper explicitly states these 45 benchmarks measure tactic-search infrastructure speed, not proof-discovery accuracy; only three problems are full end-to-end DSP runs.

claim_checks.claim: Import caching and theorem-body snapshot reuse are distinct mechanisms.
claim_checks.evidence: Kimina's primary report says its LRU cache reuses workers with matching import headers and then verifies the body. Snapshot-DSP captures after theorem-body elaboration and reuses that proof state across branches. Snapshot-DSP v2 therefore correctly distinguishes import-level environment reuse from same-theorem post-elaboration snapshot reuse; it also says the two can compose.
claim_checks.scope: Snapshot-DSP's persistent-server Level 1+2 numbers are estimates/future work, not measured implementation results.

claim_checks.evidence: The limitations section calls Snapshot-DSP a pure acceleration architecture: same tactic portfolio, same sketches, same set of proved theorems as fallback; accuracy/search strategy are unchanged.
claim_checks.scope: Any claim that snapshots themselves improve theorem-solving quality would exceed the tested evidence.

additional_scope_corrections: The current implementation restarts the LSP server per theorem, so it still pays the roughly 60 s import cost once per theorem; cross-theorem persistent-server amortization is not implemented in the reported system.
All experiments use one Apple M-series MacBook Pro with 8 GB RAM and a patched Lean 4.25.1 toolchain; other hardware and deeper/harder proof distributions were not characterized.
The paper's >100x Level 1+2 and large-branch projections are modeled estimates, not measured results and must not be mixed with the measured 5.6-50x range.

As of this audit, the paper-advertised public GitHub repository https://github.com/A2DR1/Lean_Snapshot returned 404 through the GitHub API/search path, so the numerical result is primary-paper verified but not independently reproduced from the claimed release artifact in this run.
material_note: C35 is directionally correct after narrowing. The >99% overhead and 5.6-50x speedup are real primary-paper results for Snapshot-DSP's specific rebuild-per-branch miniF2F-v2/DSP substrate. Treat theorem-body 18-735 s as estimated/back-computed, distinguish measured snapshot results from projected persistent-server combinations, and do not transfer the speedup or cost mix to a cached/persistent Lean runtime without measurement. Kimina primary evidence confirms import-header caching is a different layer from post-elaboration branch snapshots.
unresolved: Independent reproduction of Snapshot-DSP timing on the released implementation/artifacts.
